claims.statement: For the full distinguished root-plus-arm sector of CB(8,92) at p=492, ordinary rank-491-to-rank-490 deletion alone has a selected-tag weighted mass ratio 493/491, so a deletion-only capacity argument is short by 2 W_490/491; this yields a necessary whole-sector surplus threshold for switch targets under the stated weighting.
claims.scope: The CB(8,92) root-plus-arm sector with 736 disjoint support-leaf pairs, source rank 491, deletion rank 490, and weight 1 plus the number of selected branch leaves. This is not a mixed Hall theorem for arbitrary subfamilies or trees.
claims.reason: The rank and weighted-mass ratios follow by exact counting in the colored pair-choice sector. The result isolates a necessary amount of usable two-for-one switch capacity but does not establish that capacity, control overlap or competing demand, or settle the primary aggregate.

limitations: The selected-tag mass calculation is confined to one whole sector and is not an arbitrary-subfamily weighted Hall bound.
The available CB(8,92) conservative switch-cut envelope is inconclusive and does not certify a feasible flow or deficient cut.
No universal conclusion for ordinary trees follows from this bounded structural analysis.
